findings.title: limitFunction drops every call argument at runtime
findings.cause: The wrapper returned at index.js:124 is `() => limit(() => function_())`, so it never forwards `...arguments_` into the limited call.
findings.impact: Any consumer that wraps a parameterized function with the public `limitFunction` export receives `undefined` inputs at runtime. That silently corrupts results while the declaration file still advertises full argument preservation.
evidence: Runtime implementation at index.js:121-124 returns a zero-argument wrapper.
The public type contract at index.d.ts:133-136 says the returned function accepts the original `Arguments` tuple.
benchmark.js:184-195 calls `limitedTask(delay, i)`, showing the repo itself expects argument forwarding.
findings.reproduction_or_test: From the repo root, run `node --input-type=module` with `const limited = limitFunction(async (a, b) => `${String(a)}|${String(b)}`, {concurrency: 1}); console.log(await limited('left', 'right'));`. Observed output: `undefined|undefined`.

findings.title: Options-object construction flips `rejectOnClear` to enabled by default
findings.cause: When the options form is used, `({concurrency, rejectOnClear = true} = concurrency)` overwrites the documented default `false` with `true` whenever the field is omitted or `undefined`.
findings.impact: `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` and `limitFunction(fn, {concurrency: 1})` create limiters whose `clearQueue()` rejects pending work with `AbortError` instead of merely discarding it. That contradicts the README and declaration docs and can surface unexpected rejections during teardown.
evidence: index.js:4-13 initializes `rejectOnClear` to `false` and then replaces it with a destructuring default of `true` in the object branch.
index.js:77-89 routes `clearQueue()` through promise rejection whenever `rejectOnClear` is truthy.
README lines 46-52 and 104-105 document `rejectOnClear` with default `false`, and README line 57 demonstrates the object form `pLimit({concurrency: 1})`.
index.d.ts:99-106 also documents the option default as `false`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: From the repo root, run `node --input-type=module` with `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); const running = limit(() => delay(50)); const pending = limit(() => delay(10)); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); await pending;`. The pending promise rejects with `AbortError` instead of staying unresolved or being silently discarded.
